components:
 parameters:
 evalVocabularyHeader:
 name: x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary
 in:

header
 required: false
 description: >-
 Which vocabulary this request and its response speak. Absent means
`1`,\n which is byte-for-byte today's contract: the same request fields, the\n same refusals, the same response proj

ection. `2` is the canonical
 vocabulary. Any other value is a `400` with `code: "VALIDATION_ERROR"`.


 Today
it decides one thing: the spelling of an evaluator's policy\n `role`. Vocabulary 1 accepts and returns `gating`; vocabular
y 2 accepts\n both spellings and returns the canonical `required`. Sending `required`\n without the header is a `400
`, deliberately — vocabulary 1 is not\n widened to meet vocabulary 2 half way, because a boundary that accepts a\n s

pelling it does not announce is one two implementations can disagree
 about.


 A response that varies by vocabu

lary sends `Vary:
 x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`.
 schema:
 type: string
 enum:
 - '1'

- '2'
 example: '2'

 in: path

of the hosted project that contains the server.

path

 schema:
 type: str

ing
 declaredSuiteIdQuery:
 name: declaredSuiteId
 in: query
 required: false
 description: >-
The suite file's own `suite.id`, when this request is that file syncing\n itself. A CI-owned suite (see `EvalSuiteDetail.
managedBy`) refuses\n configuration writes with `409` and `details.reason:\n \"CI_OWNED_SUITE_READ_ONLY\"`; naming t
he suite's own declared id is how\n the file writing itself is allowed through. Naming any other id refuses\n exactl

y as loudly as naming none, so it is not a capability — omit it
 for an ordinary edit.


 A QUERY PARAMETER on e
very route that takes it, never a body field.\n These request bodies are strict, here and on every Inspector that\n
predates the CI-owned lock, so a body field is a `400` against an older\n deployment — which would break `mcpjam cloud eval
run --file` for anyone\n whose CLI is newer than their Inspector. A query parameter is read by\n the deployments th
at know it and ignored by those that do not, which is\n the right degradation: an Inspector with no lock has no exception t

o
 make.
 schema:
 type: string
 maxLength: 128
 schemas:
 EvalCaseCreateRequest:
 type:

object
 required:
 - title
 - steps
 description: >-
 Create one case. `title` and a non-empt

y `steps` array are both required
 — a case persisted without executable steps could never run.
 properties:

judge:
 type: object
 additionalProperties: false
 properties:
 enabled:

type: boolean
 nullable: true
 description: >-
 Per-case judge override. enabled: false skips go

al-completion
 grading for this case; null clears the override and restores the
 suite setting.
 d

eclaredSuiteId:
 type: string
 maxLength: 128
 description: >-
 The suite file's own `su

ite.id`, when THIS request is a suite-file
 sync.


 A CI-owned suite (see `EvalSuiteDetail.managedBy`)
refuses\n configuration writes with `409` and `details.reason:\n \"CI_OWNED_SUITE_READ_ONLY\"`. Naming the s
uite's own declared id is\n how the file writing itself is allowed through — the platform\n permits the writ
e only when the id matches, so naming any other id\n refuses exactly as loudly as naming none. Omit it for ordinary\n

edits.


 PREFER THE `declaredSuiteId` QUERY PARAMETER on this route. This
 body field still w
orks here, but these request bodies are strict on\n every Inspector that predates the CI-owned lock, so a body field is
\n a `400` against an older deployment while an unknown query parameter\n is simply ignored. The MCPJam SDK

and CLI send the query parameter.

ring

 Stable declared id for the case — the id i

n the suite. Distinct from the `id` on the response,

minimum: 1

 Per-case repetitions; omitted cases inherit the suite d
efault.\n PER-CASE GRADING ONLY — on a suite decided by the suite-wide\n accuracy threshold this is a VALIDA
TION_ERROR naming the criterion\n change that would make it readable, because that criterion takes the\n tri
al count from `iterations` raised to the suite's\n `minimumIterations` and would never read this. Capped at 10, the\n
same hosted ceiling as `iterations`; the suite-file contract's\n larger `MAX_REPETITIONS` is what a file may

DECLARE, not what a
 hosted run accepts.

maximum: 1

 Per-case pass threshold FRACTION: the share of this case's own
iterations that must pass. PER-CASE GRADING ONLY — on a suite\n decided by the suite-wide accuracy threshold this is a
